question: What type of polynomial does torch.linalg.eigvalsh compute the roots of for a complex Hermitian or real symmetric matrix?
reference_answer: torch.linalg.eigvalsh computes the roots of the polynomial \( p(\lambda) = \det(A - \lambda I_n) \) for a complex Hermitian or real symmetric matrix \( A \in K^n \times n \), where \( \lambda \in \mathbb{R} \).
gold_chunk_text:
PyTorch Documentation, Release main
72.2.8 torch.linalg.eigvalsh
torch.linalg.eigvalsh(A, UPLO=/quotesingle.ts1L/quotesingle.ts1, *, out=None)→ Tensor
Computes the eigenvalues of a complex Hermitian or real symmetric matrix.
Letting K be R or C, the eigenvalues of a complex Hermitian or real symmetric matrix 𝐴∈ K𝑛×𝑛 are defined
as the roots (counted with multiplicity) of the polynomial p of degree n given by
𝑝(𝜆) = det(𝐴−𝜆I𝑛) 𝜆∈ R
where I𝑛 is the n-dimensional identity matrix. The eigenvalues of a real symmetric or complex Hermitian matrix
are always real.
Supports input of float, double, cfloat and cdouble dtypes. Also supports batches of matrices, and if A is a batch
of matrices then the output has the same batch dimensions.
The eigenvalues are returned in ascending order.

reference_answer: If the function is not defined, such as sqrt(-1) or log(-1), the value used as the gradient is arbitrary. Most functions will use NaN as the gradient, but for performance reasons, some functions will use other values like log(-1).
